column1: # Game profile of Assassin's Creed: The Ezio Collection (Switch, update 1.3, v196608): Assassin's Creed II in program 0, Brotherhood in program 1 with its data as DLC
# (0100670014483001), Ubisoft's AnvilNext, NVN, SDK 11.4.3, Havok and Wwise. On the Mac this program boots through the collection's launcher parameter into II's
# menus and its opening at Abstergo, under control, at 30 fps. Its shaders are bare control sections and code areas, 160 in main and 46,540 in the Oodle blocks
# of the .forge archives of versions 31 (II) and 25 (Brotherhood) (dm/gfx/tools/anvil_forge.py; see README.md)
# The provisional profile the survey made (dm/games/profile_guess.py), with the launcher's parameter (launch_param), shader_separate and Brotherhood's shader group added
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# The collection's launcher (this program, started from HOME) restarts it with oe::ExecuteProgram(0, "/launcher:off /gamesoundlanguage:en /gamemenulanguage:en
# /gamerewardsPurchased:0  /world:TitleScreen") to start Assassin's Creed II (100 bytes, no terminating zero); the host runs one program, so it hands that parameter
# over at the start instead (hle_oe.c), and the game starts II without the launcher. Brotherhood, the launcher's other choice, is program 1 (80 bytes of parameters)
# Every shader is one stage, a control section directly followed by its code area in the .forge entries and in main, and the game draws with a vertex shader and a
# pixel shader of separate objects: every vertex shader is paired with the pixel shader cover (shader_split.py separable_pairs), so it is padded for any of them
